newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 0.50 cent per lb higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 0.50 cent per lb higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 0.50 cent per lb firmer on Wednesday, floor sources said.
Talks to end a strike by Colombia's main truck drivers' union ended late Tuesday with no agreement reached over key demands, union officials said.

CSCE coffee futures closed lower on Tuesday as speculators took profits on the market's recent surge to new two-and-a-half year highs. Benchmark July fell 5.70 cents per lb, after trading from 188 to 193 cents. Spot May eased 3.70 to 211.20.

Technically, the recent low of 187.50 basis July was viewed as a key near-term objective while further support was cited at 180 cents. To the upside, 195 and 199-200 cents were seen as major chart hurdles.
LIFFE coffee futures stood lower by the midday break, with July down $11 to $1,655.
